question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words/phrase.
Adjust or make right; correct, amend
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Rectify.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Rectify" means to adjust or make something right; to correct or amend an error or fault. (सुधारना, ठीक करना)
◦ Example: The technician was called in to rectify the fault in the wiring.

• It comes from the Latin "rectus" (right/straight) + "facere" (to make) — literally "to make right".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Recruit (भर्ती करना): To enlist or enrol a new member, especially into an organisation or the armed forces; it does not mean to correct something.

• Option 2: Recreate (पुनः निर्माण करना): To create or form again; to reproduce.

• Option 3: Recourse (सहारा): A source of help in a difficult situation; the act of turning to someone or something for assistance.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Rectify" with "Ratify" (to formally approve or confirm, e.g. a treaty) — a common SSC trap.

• Related words: rectification (noun), rectifiable (adjective).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate word. Choose the correct alternative.
Be it a chaat or a refreshing lemonade, lemon is the need of the hour in _______ summers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. scorching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "scorching" means extremely hot, burning. The sentence talks about a chaat or lemonade being needed in very hot summers, so "scorching summers" fits the context logically.

• Scorching is commonly used to describe intense heat, e.g. "a scorching afternoon", "scorching sun".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Banging" means excellent or exciting (informal slang) or a loud noise; it does not describe weather/temperature in this sense.

• Option 2: "Freezing" means extremely cold, which is the opposite of the context — cold lemonade/chaat would not specifically be called a "need of the hour" in freezing weather.

• Option 4: "Alleviating" means reducing pain or difficulty; it is a verb form and does not fit grammatically as an adjective describing "summers".

NOTE

• Words related to extreme heat often tested by SSC: sweltering, blistering, torrid, sultry.

• Words related to extreme cold: freezing, frigid, chilly, arctic.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
They will go to bed / early since they / have to get up / at five on the morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. at five on the morning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The segment "at five on the morning" contains an error in the preposition. The correct preposition to use before "the morning" (a part of the day) is "in", not "on".

• Rule: We use "in the morning/afternoon/evening" but "at night" and "on" + a specific date/day (e.g. "on Monday morning").

• Correct sentence: "They will go to bed early since they have to get up at five in the morning."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "have to get up" is grammatically correct — expresses an obligation in the simple present tense.

• Option 3: "They will go to bed" is grammatically correct — simple future tense correctly used.

• Option 4: "early since they" is grammatically correct — "since" is correctly used here as a conjunction meaning "because".

NOTE

• Common preposition confusions tested by SSC: in the morning/evening/afternoon vs at night vs at noon/midnight vs on a specific date.

• "At five" (a clock time) always takes "at", but the following phrase "the morning" needs "in".

question: Select the sentence with the appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: It has been raining till morning.
option_2: It has been raining from morning.
option_3: It has been raining by morning.
option_4: It has been raining since morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. It has been raining since morning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Since" is used with a point of time (a specific starting point, e.g. morning, 2018, Monday) to indicate when an action began, and is typically used with the Present Perfect / Present Perfect Continuous tense.

• Rule: Present Perfect Continuous: Subject + has/have + been + V-ing + since + point of time / for + period of time.

• Here, "morning" is a point/starting time, so "since morning" is correct: "It has been raining since morning."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "till morning" is incorrect here — "till" indicates an action continuing up to a point and stopping there, which contradicts "has been raining" (still continuing).

• Option 2: "from morning" is incorrect — "from" is not paired with the present perfect continuous to express a starting point in this construction; "since" is required.

• Option 3: "by morning" is incorrect — "by" indicates a deadline/point of completion, not a starting point of a continuing action.

NOTE

• "For" is used with a period/duration of time (e.g. for two hours, for a week), while "since" is used with a point of time (e.g. since Monday, since 2020, since morning).

• "Till/until" is used for an action that continues up to a point and then stops.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Our office is in the 2nd floor of the skyscraper.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. is on the 2nd floor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct preposition to indicate a floor/level of a building is "on". We say "on the 1st/2nd/3rd floor", not "in", "for", "with" or "at" the floor.

• Rule: "On" is used to show position on a surface or level, and floors of a building are treated as levels/surfaces.

• Correct sentence: "Our office is on the 2nd floor of the skyscraper."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "is for the 2nd floor" is incorrect — "for" indicates purpose or intended recipient, not location.

• Option 3: "is with the 2nd floor" is incorrect — "with" indicates accompaniment, not location on a level.

• Option 4: "is at the 2nd floor" is incorrect — "at" is used for precise points (e.g. at the door, at the entrance), not for floors/levels of a building.

NOTE

• Other common "on" usages: on the ground floor, on the terrace, on the wall, on the roof, on a bus/train/plane.

• Common "at" usages: at the corner, at the bus stop, at home, at the door.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Having or showing an excessively high opinion of one's appearance, abilities, or worth
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Vain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Vain" means having or showing an excessively high opinion of one's appearance, abilities, or worth. (घमंडी, दिखावटी)
◦ Example: He was too vain to admit that he needed help.

• It is used to describe a person who is excessively proud of their looks or achievements.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Superior (श्रेष्ठ): Higher in rank, status or quality; does not specifically mean excessive pride in appearance.

• Option 3: Otiose (व्यर्थ, निरर्थक): Serving no practical purpose; useless or futile.

• Option 4: Domineering (हावी होने वाला): Tending to control or bully others.

NOTE

• Words related to excessive pride/self-regard often confused: vain, conceited, arrogant, vainglorious, narcissistic.

• "Vain" also has another meaning — "useless/unsuccessful", as in "in vain" (without success).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence.
One must learn to __________ a line between one's private and professional life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. draw.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiomatic expression "to draw a line" (between two things) means to set or establish a clear boundary or distinction between them.

• Here, "One must learn to draw a line between one's private and professional life" means one must maintain a clear separation between the two.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "catch" does not collocate with "a line" in this sense; "catch a line" is not an idiomatic expression meaning to set a boundary.

• Option 3: "bring" does not fit the idiomatic collocation "___ a line between".

• Option 4: "get" does not fit the idiomatic collocation "___ a line between".

NOTE

• Related expressions: "to draw the line at something" (to refuse to go beyond a certain limit), "a fine line between" (a subtle distinction).

• Other fixed verb + noun collocations tested by SSC: make a decision, take a break, come to a conclusion, keep a promise.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
The date when both, day and night are of approximately equal length
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Equinox.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Equinox" means the date when both day and night are of approximately equal length, occurring twice a year (around 20-21 March and 22-23 September). (विषुव — जब दिन और रात बराबर होते हैं)
◦ Example: The autumn equinox marks the change of season.

• It comes from Latin "aequus" (equal) + "nox" (night).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Equilibrium (संतुलन): A state of balance, especially between opposing forces or influences.

• Option 2: Equine (घोड़े से संबंधित): Relating to horses.

• Option 3: Equator (भूमध्य रेखा): The imaginary line around the earth equidistant from the North and South Poles.

NOTE

• Related word: "Solstice" — the day when the sun reaches its highest or lowest point in the sky, resulting in the longest or shortest day of the year.

• Both "equinox" and "solstice" occur twice a year (spring/autumn equinox; summer/winter solstice).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Beat around the bush
option_2: Avoid the main point by talking in a roundabout way
option_3: Avoid saying what you mean, usually because it is not funny
option_4: Avoid using foul words to make someone uncomfortable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Avoid the main point by talking in a roundabout way.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Beat around the bush" means to avoid talking about the main point or issue directly, instead talking in a vague or roundabout way. (घुमा-फिरा कर बात करना, मुद्दे से बचना)
◦ Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened.

• The idiom originates from hunting, where beaters would beat the bushes to flush birds out, working around the edges before getting to the actual target.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Avoid praising someone and demean" does not match the meaning of this idiom.

• Option 3: "Avoid saying what you mean, usually because it is not funny" is not the meaning of this idiom — this description does not correspond to any standard idiom meaning here.

• Option 4: "Avoid using foul words to make someone uncomfortable" does not match the meaning of this idiom.

NOTE

• Other idioms of evasiveness commonly asked in SSC: "To beat about the bush" (same as beat around the bush), "To hedge one's bets", "To skirt around an issue", "To dodge the question".

• Opposite idiom: "To come straight to the point" / "To call a spade a spade" (to speak frankly and directly).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Beneth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Beneath" (meaning "under" or "below"), not "Beneth". The word "Beneth" as given is incorrectly spelt.

• Spelling key: BE + NEATH — remember the "ea" in the middle, as in "neat" plus "h".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Belief" is correctly spelt — remember "i before e" here: B-E-L-I-E-F.

• Option 3: "Belly" is correctly spelt.

• Option 4: "Bellow" is correctly spelt (meaning to roar loudly, or a device for blowing air).

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Beneath" (below) with "Benefit" or "Beneficent", which have different roots.

• Other commonly misspelt words with silent/tricky vowel combinations: wreath, sheath, breathe, underneath.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Regardless of their diversity, all flowers have a uniform function, the reproduction of the species through the production of seed.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Uniformity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "diversity" means the state of being diverse, varied, or having many different types/forms.

• Its antonym is "Uniformity", which means the state of being the same or unvarying; sameness. (एकरूपता, समानता — diversity का विलोम)

• The sentence itself supports this: "...all flowers have a uniform function..." — "uniformity" is the noun form of "uniform", the direct opposite of "diversity" (variety).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Melancholy (उदासी): A feeling of deep, pensive sadness — unrelated to variety/sameness.

• Option 2: Equilibrium (संतुलन): A state of balance; not an antonym of diversity.

• Option 3: Affinity (आत्मीयता, समानता का भाव): A natural liking or kinship for someone/something; it is actually closer to a synonym of similarity than an antonym of diversity, but does not directly mean "sameness/uniformity" in the way required here.

NOTE

• Synonyms of "diversity": variety, multiplicity, heterogeneity.

• Other antonym pairs often tested: heterogeneous ↔ homogeneous, varied ↔ uniform, diverse ↔ identical.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.
Visiting a book fair always fills my heart with a great satisfaction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. contentment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined word "satisfaction" means a feeling of pleasure or fulfilment derived from something.

• Its closest synonym here is "contentment", meaning a state of peaceful happiness and satisfaction. (संतोष)

• In the sentence, visiting a book fair gives the speaker a feeling of contented pleasure/fulfilment, which "contentment" captures precisely.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "refreshment" (ताज़गी): A feeling of being refreshed or renewed, or food/drink; does not mean satisfaction.

• Option 2: "pride" (गर्व): A feeling of deep pleasure from one's own achievements, not the same as satisfaction from an external experience.

• Option 4: "bliss" (परम आनंद): Extreme or perfect happiness; too strong/intense a word compared to the moderate "satisfaction" in context.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "satisfaction": gratification, fulfilment, contentedness.

• Antonyms of "satisfaction": dissatisfaction, discontent, frustration.

question:
Select the correct active form of the given sentence.
Was the message given by him?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Did he give the message?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence "Was the message given by him?" is a passive interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense (Interrogative):
◦ Passive: Was/Were + Object + V3 + by + Subject?
◦ Active: Did + Subject + V1 + Object?

• Applying the rule: the agent "him" becomes the subject "he"; the passive verb "was given" becomes "did...give" (V1 form after "did"); and "the message" (object of passive) becomes the object of the active sentence.
◦ Active: Did he give the message?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Was he given the message?" is incorrect — this is still a passive construction (with "he" as the recipient), not the correct active form.

• Option 2: "Does he give the message?" is incorrect — it wrongly uses the simple present tense instead of the simple past tense.

• Option 3: "Did he gave the message?" is incorrect — after the auxiliary "did", the main verb must be in its base form (V1) "give", not the past form "gave".

NOTE

• After auxiliary verbs like "did", "does", "do", the main verb always takes the base form (V1) — never V2/V3.

• Common error: using "did + V2" together (e.g. "did he gave/went/ate") — this is a frequently tested SSC trap.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Deliberate
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Planned.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Deliberate" (adjective) means done consciously and intentionally; carefully thought out or planned in advance. (जानबूझकर, सोच-समझकर किया गया)

• Its closest synonym is "Planned", meaning arranged or decided in advance, which matches the sense of intentionality in "deliberate".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Casual" (लापरवाह, अनौपचारिक): Relaxed, informal, or done without much thought — nearly opposite to "deliberate".

• Option 2: "Hasty" (जल्दबाज़ी में किया गया): Done with excessive speed and without careful thought — opposite in meaning to "deliberate".

• Option 4: "Rushed" (जल्दी में किया गया): Done in a hurry, without proper care — opposite in meaning to "deliberate".

NOTE

• "Deliberate" can also be a verb (di-LIB-er-ate) meaning "to think about or discuss something carefully" — note the difference in pronunciation and part of speech from the adjective (di-LIB-er-it).

• Synonyms of "deliberate" (adjective): intentional, calculated, premeditated, conscious.

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.
She said, "She must leave all the bad habits."
option_1: She said she has to leave all the bad habits
option_2: She said that she must have leave all the bad habits
option_3: She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.
option_4: She said that she could leave all the bad habits
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given direct sentence is: She said, "She must leave all the bad habits."

• Rule — Reported Speech with "must": When "must" expresses obligation/necessity (not certainty/inference), it is changed to "had to" in indirect speech.

• Applying the rule: "must leave" → "had to leave"; the reporting verb "said" (no object) stays as "said that"; and the pronoun "She" (subject of the quoted sentence) is retained as "she" since the reference is consistent.
◦ Indirect: She said that she had to leave all the bad habits.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "She said she has to leave all the bad habits" is incorrect — the present tense "has to" is wrong; since the reporting verb "said" is in the past tense, the reported verb must also shift backward in time ("had to").

• Option 2: "She said that she must have leave all the bad habits" is incorrect — "must have leave" is grammatically malformed and does not correctly represent "must" in reported speech.

• Option 4: "She said that she could leave all the bad habits" is incorrect — "could" expresses ability/permission, not obligation, and thus distorts the original meaning of "must" (obligation).

NOTE

• "Must" changes to "had to" when expressing obligation, but remains "must" when expressing logical certainty/inference (e.g. "He must be tired" stays "He said he must be tired").

• Other modal changes in reported speech: can → could, may → might, will → would, shall → should.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Magnify
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Expand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Magnify" means to make something appear larger than it actually is, or to increase its size/effect. (बड़ा करना, आवर्धित करना)

• Its closest synonym is "Expand", meaning to increase in size, extent or scope.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Magnanimous" (उदार): Generous or forgiving, especially towards a rival or less powerful person — an unrelated adjective despite the similar spelling to "magnify".

• Option 3: "Miniature" (लघु रूप): A very small copy or model of something — this is close to the opposite of "magnify".

• Option 4: "Underemphasise": To give too little emphasis or importance to something — opposite in meaning to "magnify".

NOTE

• Do not confuse "Magnify" (to enlarge) with "Magnanimous" (generous) — they share the root "magnus" (great) but differ in meaning.

• Synonyms of "magnify": amplify, enlarge, augment, intensify. Antonyms: minimise, diminish, reduce.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Avariciuos.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Avaricious" (meaning extremely greedy for wealth), not "Avariciuos". The letters "u" and "o" have been wrongly interchanged in the given word.

• Spelling key: AVARICE + -IOUS → Avaricious. Remember the ending is "-ious", not "-iuos".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Clemency" is correctly spelt (meaning mercy or leniency).

• Option 3: "Hegemony" is correctly spelt (meaning dominance of one group/state over others).

• Option 4: "Nostalgic" is correctly spelt (meaning feeling a sentimental longing for the past).

NOTE

• The noun form is "avarice" (greed), and the adjective is "avaricious".

• Other adjectives ending in "-ious" commonly tested: ambitious, cautious, gracious, malicious, suspicious.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
All his friends laughed at him.
option_1: He became laughable to his friends.
option_2: He was laughed at by all his friends.
option_3: His friends were being laughed at by him.
option_4: All his friends were laughing at him.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. He was laughed at by all his friends.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "All his friends laughed at him" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Past Tense, with the phrasal verb "laughed at".

• Rule — Passive of Phrasal Verbs: With phrasal verbs like "laugh at", "look after", "look into" etc., the preposition/particle must stay attached to the verb even in the passive voice.
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + (particle) + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "him" becomes the subject "He"; the verb "laughed at" becomes "was laughed at"; and "all his friends" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: He was laughed at by all his friends.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "He became laughable to his friends" is incorrect — this changes the meaning and structure entirely rather than forming a correct grammatical passive of the given sentence.

• Option 3: "His friends were being laughed at by him" is incorrect — this reverses the subject and object, producing the opposite meaning (that he laughed at his friends).

• Option 4: "All his friends were laughing at him" is incorrect — this is simply the sentence rewritten in the Past Continuous active voice, not a passive construction.

NOTE

• When converting phrasal verbs to passive voice, never drop the preposition/particle (at, after, into, up to, etc.) — a very common SSC trap.

• Other examples: "They looked after the child" → "The child was looked after (by them)"; "She laughed at the joke" → "The joke was laughed at (by her)".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
One who has the ability to do many different things
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Versatile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Versatile" means one who has the ability to do many different things competently. (बहुमुखी प्रतिभा वाला)
◦ Example: She is a versatile actress who can perform comedy, drama and action roles equally well.

• It emphasises range and adaptability across multiple skills or fields, not just skill in one area.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Adaptable (अनुकूलनशील): Able to adjust to new conditions; refers to flexibility in changing circumstances, not necessarily the ability to do many different things.

• Option 3: Expert (विशेषज्ञ): A person with a very high level of skill/knowledge in one particular area — the opposite emphasis of "versatile" (breadth vs. depth).

• Option 4: Specialist (विशेषज्ञ): A person who concentrates on and is highly skilled in one particular subject/activity — again, the opposite emphasis of "versatile".

NOTE

• Related word: "Versatility" (noun) — the quality of being versatile.

• Do not confuse "versatile" (many skills) with "specialist"/"expert" (one skill, deeply) — SSC often pairs these as contrasting options.

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
There are
P. reports that toy shops and other
Q. to prepare for the Christmas rush
R. non-food retailers are struggling to
S. get enough stock into their warehouses
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. PRSQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence begins with the fixed opener "There are", which needs a subject/noun phrase to follow logically — P. "reports that toy shops and other" fits directly, introducing "reports" as the subject.

• Part P ("...toy shops and other") logically connects to R ("non-food retailers are struggling to"), continuing the noun phrase "toy shops and other non-food retailers" as the subject of "are struggling to".

• Part R ("...struggling to") logically connects to S ("get enough stock into their warehouses"), completing the infinitive "struggling to get enough stock...".

• Part S logically connects to Q ("to prepare for the Christmas rush"), giving the purpose/reason for getting stock into warehouses.
◦ Full sentence: "There are reports that toy shops and other non-food retailers are struggling to get enough stock into their warehouses to prepare for the Christmas rush."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 (PRSQ).

Additional Information

• Option 1 (RPSQ) is incorrect because it starts with "non-food retailers are struggling to", which cannot logically follow "There are" without first introducing "reports that toy shops and other...".

• Option 3 (SQRP) is incorrect because it breaks the required subject-verb sequence, placing "get enough stock" before the subject "toy shops and other non-food retailers" is even introduced.

• Option 4 (QRPS) is incorrect because it places the purpose clause "to prepare for the Christmas rush" before the subject and main clause are established, making the sentence incoherent.

NOTE

• In parajumble/sentence-rearrangement questions, always look for a grammatical subject to follow the fixed opener, and track pronoun/connector clues (like "to", "and") that link parts together.

• Here, "and other" (end of P) is a strong clue that another noun phrase (R: "non-food retailers") must follow immediately.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.

Memory loss, with aging, is (1)_______ a natural and normal (2)_______. The symptoms range from forgetting simple daily life activities and (3)_______ familiar tasks such as driving or baking. However, there can be several other factors (4)_______ for it and these vary from person to person. Memory loss can be (5)______ or total depending upon the condition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. considered.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that completes the passive construction **"is ___ a natural and normal process"**, meaning memory loss is regarded/thought of as natural.

• "Considered" fits correctly: "is considered" = is regarded/thought to be — a standard passive collocation ("X is considered a natural process").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "consider" is incorrect — it is the base form (V1) and cannot follow "is" directly in this passive-like construction ("is consider" is ungrammatical).

• Option 2: "denied" is incorrect — "is denied a natural process" does not make logical sense in context; "denied" means refused/rejected, which contradicts the passage's meaning.

• Option 3: "regard" is incorrect — like "consider", it is a base verb form and cannot follow "is" directly; the correct form would need to be "regarded".

NOTE

• Common passive collocations: "is considered", "is regarded as", "is viewed as", "is seen as" — all followed by a noun/adjective complement.

• After the auxiliary "is/am/are/was/were" in a passive sense, the main verb must be in its past participle (V3) form.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.

Memory loss, with aging, is (1)_______ a natural and normal (2)_______. The symptoms range from forgetting simple daily life activities and (3)_______ familiar tasks such as driving or baking. However, there can be several other factors (4)_______ for it and these vary from person to person. Memory loss can be (5)______ or total depending upon the condition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. process.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a noun describing what memory loss (with aging) is considered to be: **"a natural and normal ___"**.

• "Process" fits best — memory loss with age is described as a natural and normal biological/physiological process (an ongoing series of changes).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "trial" means a test or a difficult experience; it does not fit the sense of a natural, ongoing bodily change.

• Option 2: "type" means a category or kind; it does not make sense to say something is "a natural and normal type" without specifying "type of what".

• Option 3: "method" means a systematic way of doing something; memory loss is not a "method", so this does not fit contextually.

NOTE

• Words like "process", "phenomenon", "occurrence" are commonly used in passages describing natural/biological changes.

• "Process" implies gradual, ongoing change — appropriate for describing aging-related memory loss.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.

Memory loss, with aging, is (1)_______ a natural and normal (2)_______. The symptoms range from forgetting simple daily life activities and (3)_______ familiar tasks such as driving or baking. However, there can be several other factors (4)_______ for it and these vary from person to person. Memory loss can be (5)______ or total depending upon the condition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. performing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"forgetting simple daily life activities and ___ familiar tasks such as driving or baking"**, describing the range of memory-loss symptoms.

• "Performing" fits best — the sentence lists symptoms as forgetting daily activities and (having trouble) performing familiar tasks like driving or baking, i.e. the act of carrying out these tasks becomes affected.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "prospering" means thriving or succeeding financially; it does not fit the context of memory-related symptoms.

• Option 2: "acknowledging" means accepting or admitting something; it does not fit the description of forgetting/struggling with tasks.

• Option 3: "rectifying" means correcting or fixing an error; it does not describe carrying out familiar tasks like driving or baking.

NOTE

• In this context, "performing familiar tasks" means the physical/mental act of carrying out routine, well-known activities.

• Words describing carrying out tasks: performing, executing, carrying out, undertaking.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.

Memory loss, with aging, is (1)_______ a natural and normal (2)_______. The symptoms range from forgetting simple daily life activities and (3)_______ familiar tasks such as driving or baking. However, there can be several other factors (4)_______ for it and these vary from person to person. Memory loss can be (5)______ or total depending upon the condition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. responsible.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"there can be several other factors ___ for it"**, describing factors that cause or lead to memory loss.

• "Responsible" fits correctly — the fixed collocation "factors responsible for" means causes/reasons that bring about a particular effect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "commendable" means praiseworthy or deserving approval; it does not fit the sense of "causing" memory loss.

• Option 3: "affluent" means having a great deal of wealth; it is unrelated to the context of causes of memory loss.

• Option 4: "significance" is a noun, not an adjective, and cannot correctly follow "factors ___ for it" in this construction; also it does not convey causation.

NOTE

• Fixed collocation: "factors responsible for" / "reasons responsible for" — very commonly tested in SSC cloze passages.

• Do not confuse "responsible for" (causing) with "responsive to" (reacting to).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.

Memory loss, with aging, is (1)_______ a natural and normal (2)_______. The symptoms range from forgetting simple daily life activities and (3)_______ familiar tasks such as driving or baking. However, there can be several other factors (4)_______ for it and these vary from person to person. Memory loss can be (5)______ or total depending upon the condition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. partial.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank completes the phrase **"Memory loss can be ___ or total depending upon the condition"**, contrasting two possible degrees/extents of memory loss.

• "Partial" fits correctly as it is grammatically parallel to "total" (both are adjectives describing the extent/degree of memory loss) and gives the logical contrast "partial or total" (some vs. complete memory loss).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "partially" is incorrect — it is an adverb, and cannot be grammatically parallel to the adjective "total" in the construction "___ or total".

• Option 3: "completely" is incorrect — it is an adverb, not an adjective, and does not logically pair with "total" either (also creates near-redundant meaning with "total").

• Option 4: "incomplete" is incorrect — while it is an adjective, "incomplete or total" does not form as natural or standard a contrast as "partial or total" in describing degree of memory loss.

NOTE

• When a blank must be grammatically parallel to a given word joined by "or"/"and", check the part of speech match carefully (adjective with adjective, noun with noun, etc.).

• Common contrastive adjective pairs: partial/total, temporary/permanent, minor/major.
